traceability.notes:
The story docs/stories/021.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-AUTO-FIX.story.md describe two main capabilities: (1) inserting a file-level @supports template with clear placeholders when missing, and (2) auto-fixing malformed [REQ-XXX] prefixes in test names, with strict safety, no semantic inference, and good developer experience. The require-test-traceability rule and its helpers implement these behaviors:
- File-level template: ensureFileSupportsAnnotation detects missing @supports and, when autoFixTestTemplate is true, uses insertSupportsTemplate + buildSupportsTemplateComment to insert a JSDoc block at the top of the file (or just after a shebang). The default template uses an obviously placeholder story path and REQ IDs and includes a TODO line explaining exactly what to replace, satisfying REQ-TEST-FIX-TEMPLATE, REQ-TEST-FIX-PLACEHOLDER, and REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE. - Prefix format fixes: normalizeReqPrefixInDescription and normalizeReqId correct spacing, delimiters, and casing for existing REQ IDs in test names, and handle brackets vs. parentheses. They never invent new IDs and only operate when a recognizable REQ prefix is already present, satisfying REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT and REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE. - Safety and preservation: All fixes are limited to comment insertion and string literal replacement; createUpdatedStringLiteralRaw preserves quote style and escaping, and shebang handling preserves executable semantics. The code guards fixer creation behind multiple safety checks, satisfying REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE and REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE. - Integration and UX: The rule is configured with meta.fixable="code" and default auto-fix options, integrates naturally with ESLint --fix, and is covered by a dedicated RuleTester suite that exercises both valid and invalid auto-fix scenarios for 021.0. User-facing docs in user-docs/api-reference.md describe the auto-fix behaviors, configuration options, and templates. Jest test output confirms all require-test-traceability tests pass.
All acceptance criteria and per-requirement behaviors from Story 021.0 are implemented, tested, and documented; therefore the story is fully satisfied.
